newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Commercial banks keep Dutch call rates high.
newsitem.headline: Commercial banks keep Dutch call rates high.

text.p: Dutch call money rates stuck at highs on Friday as commercial banks sought to eliminate their overdraft under the secured loans quota.
The Dutch central bank sets a regular quota on the amount commercial banks may borrow in secured loans at the lowest available rate, which is currently two percent.
Commercial banks have exceeded their daily average under the secured loans facility in recent days, and dealers said they were now seeking to make up the difference.
"Surprisingly call money was stuck at a high level for another day," said one.
"Banks who have eaten up some of their credit facility under the secured loans pact might be making up the difference today," he said, explaining the high level.
He said overnight money was likely to slip nearer the advances rate of 2.50 percent from the beginning of next week.
Earlier this week banks were somewhat short of liquidity, as the allocation under the previous special advances pact was not sufficient.
Dealers said that this morning's allocation of 3.74 billion guilders under a six-day pact should be enough in the following days.
Call money was bid between 2.81-2.87 percent.
Other rates rose fractionally, reflecting the market's perception that no further rate cuts are to be expected.
Dealers said the idea that no further easing of rates was to be expected followed remarks from Bundesbank officials.
"But, a rate hike should not be expected in the near-term," said one dealer. He added that money market rates were likely to stay around current levels for some more time.
Three-month deposits added two basis points to 2.96 percent bid. The guilder was steady at 112.18 per 100 marks.
